os-22-28.alt: A drawing of a capillary running diagonally between tissue cells, with two red blood cells inside it. An arrow carries carbon dioxide from a tissue cell at the top into one red blood cell, where the equation CO2 plus H2O gives H2CO3, which gives HCO3 minus plus H plus, is written; an arrow then leads from that cell into the plasma. A second arrow carries carbon dioxide from a tissue cell at the bottom into the plasma. Three labels name the forms: carbon dioxide carried in the red blood cell, bicarbonate in the plasma, and carbon dioxide dissolved in plasma.
